_source: Direct crawl of the live site on 2026-10-23, entered from the homepage and followed by internal links, not from any sitemap. Every row below was fetched. This file supersedes live-inventory.json.
method: Brightdata scrape_as_markdown / scrape_as_html / scrape_batch. The sandbox egress proxy blocks asiancoding.com directly, so every fetch went through Brightdata.

hosts.relationship: The apex 301-redirects to www (verified 2026-10-23 from the response chain), so the preferred host IS resolved. Corrected on 2026-10-23: an earlier reading of this file said neither redirected, which was wrong — a scraper following redirects silently made both hosts look independently reachable.

Auth-gated admin view of submitted requests. Should not be indexed.

Serves OpenAI's own 'Welcome back' sign-in page under the asiancoding.com origin. Flagged for the Owner: a third-party credential form on ACS's own domain is a trust and phishing-surface question, not an SEO one.
ACS Sales Desk, listing customer requests for follow-up. Found 2026-10-23 through a link on /planning-inbox; it is not linked from any public page. See DEF-08 -- urgent, and not an SEO finding.

backend.finding: GET /api/cart returns 200. The site has a real server-side API, not just static hosting.
backend.observed: 2026-10-23, in the request chain of both / and /products
backend.relevance: Server-rendering product pages is therefore feasible on the existing stack — see packages/site-fixes/PRODUCT_URL_SPEC.md §1.
backend.note: The endpoint itself could not be read; Brightdata declines it under robots.txt without KYC.

defects.finding: The sitemap is gone. /sitemap.xml and /sitemap_index.xml both 404, and robots.txt carries no Sitemap: directive.
defects.consequence: Nothing tells a crawler what the site contains.

defects.finding: 81 of the 82 URLs in the old sitemap return 404. Only / survives.
defects.consequence: Every inbound link, bookmark and indexed result pointing at the old structure lands on a 404 with no redirect.

defects.finding: 6 distinct pages are each served at 2 addresses, with and without .html, both returning 200 with identical content and no canonical tag. app.js rewrites the address bar from /products to /products.html client-side, which no crawler sees.
defects.consequence: Two-way duplication per page with no signal naming the preferred form. Downgraded from high on 2026-10-23: the apex-vs-www half of this was wrong, since the apex 301s to www.

defects.finding: The live catalogue links to ACS's own dead pages. catalog-data.js sends 5 of 14 products to www.asiancoding.com paths that 404: /ads/barcode-scanner, /brady/printers/m510, /rfid-systems, /barcode-printers, /barcode-ribbons.
defects.consequence: Customers clicking 'ดูข้อมูลหมวดสินค้าจาก ACS' reach a 404. All five were fetched and confirmed.

defects.finding: The footer on every page links to https://www.asiancoding.com/contact, which 404s.
defects.consequence: A site-wide broken link on the highest-intent navigation item.

defects.finding: The 14 products have no URLs. Detail opens in a <dialog>.
defects.consequence: No product page can rank, and no product content is crawlable. The catalogue is the only product surface and its grid is client-side.

defects.finding: /commerce-lab is an indexable, self-declared simulation carrying sample prices and stock.
defects.consequence: Sample pricing is publicly crawlable. Relevant to CR-03 even though ACS did not author it as a price claim.

defects.finding: /sales is an ACS Sales Desk page listing customer requests. It returns 200 to an unauthenticated request, carries no robots meta so it is indexable, and unlike /erp and /planning-inbox its served HTML contains no authentication gate at all. /erp ships a div id=auth-screen that blocks the shell until auth resolves, and /planning-inbox renders a permissions-check message with a sign-in link. /sales renders straight into div id=sales-list.
defects.not_verified: Whether the endpoint that fills that list requires authentication. I did NOT attempt to load the customer data: pulling real customer records to confirm an exposure would itself be the harm. The page shell being public is established. The data being public is NOT established and must be checked by someone with the right to see it.
defects.why_it_matters: If the backing endpoint authorises by session, this is only a missing noindex. If it does not, customer names, companies, emails, phone numbers and addresses submitted through /cart and /assessment are reachable without signing in.
defects.owner_action: From a signed-out browser, check the endpoint commerce.js calls for /sales. Add noindex to /sales either way.
defects.also: /sales loads catalog-data.js?v=4 while every other page loads ?v=5, so it renders against a stale catalogue, and its meta description is copy-pasted from the products page.

catalogue.note: Each product carries an `evidence` field with values acs_named_model, manufacturer_reference or acs_named_family. That is the site's own provenance marking and is worth reusing in the claim register rather than inventing a parallel scheme.

_addresses_note: Paths are relative to https://www.asiancoding.com, the host the apex 301s to. The apex forms are not listed separately because they redirect.

hosting.platform: ChatGPT sites hosting (*.chatgpt.site), fronted by Cloudflare
hosting.confidence: High, from converging evidence rather than a single header.
evidence: https://yacht369.chatgpt.site/ returns the PLATFORM 404 -- '404 Not found / No site here' -- serving /_sites/dispatch-assets/404-petlost.gif. That /_sites/ namespace is host infrastructure, not an ACS path.
acs-portal-six.yacht369.chatgpt.site serves the ACS HR Portal, so yacht369 is the ACS workspace subdomain and sites deploy as <name>.yacht369.chatgpt.site.
asiancoding.com exposes /signin-with-chatgpt and /signout-with-chatgpt on its own origin, with ?return_to= parameters. That is platform-provided ChatGPT identity, not something a static site has.
GET /api/cart returns 200, so the platform serves server-side endpoints alongside static files.
The 404 body on asiancoding.com is the platform default, which is why it looks like Next.js while every real page is hand-written static HTML with no _next assets anywhere.
hosting.ruled_out: No matching repo among the three reachable on GitHub; neither Lovable workspace; zero Vercel projects; one unrelated Netlify project; zero WordPress.com sites.
hosting.what_this_means_for_edits: catalog-data.js is a static file in this deployment. To apply packages/site-fixes/DEAD_LINK_FIX_SPEC.md, edit it wherever the yacht369 ChatGPT workspace manages this site. This session has no API access to that platform.
hosting.not_a_framework_app: Every page fetched is hand-written HTML plus plain CSS/JS: styles.css, app.js, catalog-data.js, commerce.js, planning.css/js, erp.css/js, accounting.js, integration-hub.js. planning.js imports ./planning-contract.js, ./planning-controller.js and ./planning-content.js, so the source is ES modules rather than a bundle.

robots_meta._method: Read from the served HTML head of each page on 2026-10-23. 'not read' means the page was fetched as markdown only, so its head was not inspected.
